clue.text: Fine legs, then? Some doubt emerges!

parts.note: these two words are what you get when the letters of the second word of the answer are jumbled, the first word of the answer acting as the anagram signal

explanation.surface: A cricket question about fielding positions at fine leg, followed by a cry of uncertainty.
explanation.walkthrough: A reverse clue: read the answer as wordplay, 'mixed' being an anagram signal and its fodder rearranging to FINE LEGS. 'Fine leg' is a cricket fielding position behind the batsman on the leg side.
explanation.definitionFit: Being torn between two reactions is an idiom for holding some uncertainty or ambivalence.

clue.text: Twinkling people added to corporation's impetus

indicators.note: added to says the earlier pieces are placed in front of the next one

parts.note: a twinkling is a very short moment, informally a mo
men is a plain word for people
corporation is an old jokey word for a pot belly, a tum

explanation.surface: A business tale of people joining a corporation and giving it drive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Corporation' is the old humorous British word for a paunch, hence TUM; the 's is just 'is' joining the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Momentum is the driving force or impulse that keeps something moving, a close synonym.

clue.text: Reproduced in spandex — or expensive material — that's revolutionary

indicators.note: revolutionary means turned right round, so the letters found are read backwards
in says the letters sit inside the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: Clothing made in stretchy spandex or some pricier fabric is described as a radical new fashion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that's revolutionary' turns DEXOREX, found in 'spandex or expensive', back to front; 'material' only dresses the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: To photocopy something is to copy or reproduce it, the trade name used as a verb.

clue.text: Clip weed and tie up in enclosure

definitions.meaning: to clip a tail or wages is to cut them short
a broad-leaved weed of the genus Rumex, rubbed on nettle stings
to moor a ship at a quay
the enclosed place where the accused stands in a court

explanation.surface: A gardener's job list: trim, weed, and tie plants up inside the fenced plot.
explanation.definitionFit: The one word can mean cut short, a common weed, to moor a boat, and the prisoner's enclosure in court.

clue.text: See 1
Unexpectedly Ritz reopens, even though short of volume, in initially depressed area

indicators.note: unexpectedly suggests things turning out differently, so these letters are rearranged
short of says a letter is missing from the word even

explanation.surface: The Ritz hotel surprisingly reopens in a run-down district, though business is quiet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short of volume' takes V from EVEN to leave EEN; RITZREOPENS plus EEN then rearranges into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Such a zone is an area, usually economically depressed to begin with, given tax breaks to attract business.

clue.text: Mischief that's often in the ascendant

definitions.meaning: a prank or bit of fun
a songbird famous for rising high as it sings

explanation.surface: Mischief that keeps gaining the upper hand.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means a frolic or spree, and also the skylark, which sings as it climbs.

clue.text: Currently with us — or not?

parts.note: currently means at this time, now
with us means present in this place, here

explanation.surface: A puzzled question about whether someone is present at the moment.
explanation.walkthrough: Split one way the letters say 'present at this moment'; run together they say 'in no place', which is the 'or not?'.
explanation.definitionFit: The run-together word means in no place at all, the opposite of being present.

clue.text: Star's raised a notch

indicators.note: raised means lifted up, which in a down answer means read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: our star is the sun, and the 's stands for is

explanation.surface: A celebrity's standing has gone up a notch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Star's' is read as SUN IS; 'raised' turns those letters upwards in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: In botany and anatomy the word names a rounded notch or cavity, as between lobes of a leaf.

clue.text: Mass advance around long, untidy allotment

indicators.note: around says the first word is split to wrap around what follows

parts.note: to advance is to come forward

indicators.note: untidy means messed up, so the letters of long are jumbled

parts.note: a ration is an allotted share

explanation.surface: Someone goes forward around a large, messy garden plot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'untidy' scrambles the word long to NGLO, and 'around' splits the advance word to wrap it. An allotment is a British rented vegetable plot, but here it means a share.
explanation.definitionFit: A mass of things heaped together is a jumbled cluster or accumulation, a synonym.

clue.text: Some may be bound to book for destination on the Med

definitions.text: Some may be bound to book
definitions.meaning: a fine goatskin leather used to bind books
a North African country with a Mediterranean coastline

explanation.surface: Travellers heading for the Mediterranean are certain to make a booking.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a fine leather used in bookbinding and a North African country by the Mediterranean.

clue.text: Add handy way to start play from the wings?

definitions.meaning: to include something extra, as a bonus

definitions.text: handy way to start play from the wings?
definitions.meaning: in football the ball is restarted by hand from the touchline

explanation.surface: An extra theatrical tip on how to begin a performance from the side of the stage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Play' and 'wings' suggest theatre, but this is football: the ball goes back into play thrown by hand from the touchline, so 'handy'.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb phrase it means include as an extra; as a noun it is football's restart thrown from the touchline.

clue.text: Following unknown into trap

indicators.note: into says one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a net is a trap for fish or birds
in algebra x is the classic unknown

explanation.surface: Something unidentified walks into a snare.
explanation.definitionFit: Following and the answer both mean coming immediately after, so they are synonyms.

clue.text: No navy wool in market

indicators.note: no means without, so the letter for navy is dropped

parts.note: angora is wool from the Angora goat or rabbit

explanation.surface: No navy-blue wool is on sale in the market.
explanation.definitionFit: In ancient Greece this was the open public square that served as the market place.

clue.text: Trifle with beak? It'll cost you!

parts.note: to trifle with something is to mess with it
a bird's beak is its bill

explanation.surface: A warning that dallying with a magistrate (British slang 'beak') will be expensive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Beak' is British slang for a magistrate, but here it is the bird's bill; the answer is a military officers' dining account.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the charge officers pay for meals in their mess, so it is a cost to them.

clue.text: Moonshine cloven through starlit pier

indicators.note: cloven means split, so the words are split up and only every other letter is kept

explanation.surface: Moonlight falls through the gap in a pier on a starry night.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cloven' keeps the even letters of 'starlit pier'; 'through' just joins. 'Moonshine' wants to be moonlight or illicit liquor, but here it means nonsense.
explanation.definitionFit: Moonshine can mean foolish talk, and the answer is a common word for rubbish or nonsense.

clue.text: Clubs with society gossip — it makes one weep!

parts.note: C is the card-suit abbreviation for clubs
gas is idle chatter or gossip

explanation.surface: Club members trade society tittle-tattle so cruel it brings tears.
explanation.definitionFit: This riot-control agent irritates the eyes and makes people shed tears.

clue.text: Hungry? Rescheduled dinner hour's due

indicators.note: rescheduled means rearranged, so these letters are put in a new order

explanation.surface: A diner is told the meal has been moved and is due later.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone lacking adequate food over time is underfed, an extreme form of being hungry.

clue.text: Bump into Miss Davis, perhaps, in dark

indicators.note: into puts one piece inside the other, doing double duty with the bump phrase

parts.note: Bette Davis was a Hollywood star, so Miss Davis may be Bette
to bump into someone is to run into them

explanation.surface: Running into film star Bette Davis in the darkness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bump into' is the idiom for meeting by chance; 'into' does double duty, completing the idiom and signalling the insertion.
explanation.definitionFit: A person with dark brown hair is described this way, so it means dark-haired.

clue.text: Upstart paparazzo pursuing jockey, maybe

indicators.note: pursuing means following behind, so this piece comes after the other

parts.note: a jockey may use a whip, so is a whipper
a paparazzo is a press photographer, a snapper

explanation.surface: A paparazzo chases a jockey for a photo.
explanation.definitionFit: An impertinent, presumptuous young person is an upstart, a fair synonym.

clue.text: Matt sadly deserts crumbling stately home — one for a cleric?

indicators.note: crumbling means falling to bits, so the letters of the stately home are broken up and rearranged once the other letters go

explanation.surface: Matt sadly leaves a decaying grand country house, perhaps one fit for a vicar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'deserts' and 'sadly' say the letters of MATT, in any order, leave STATELY HOME; 'crumbling' rearranges what remains. A stately home is a grand British country house.
explanation.definitionFit: The papal jurisdiction in Rome is a see, the seat of a bishop, so the question mark points to a churchman's see.

clue.text: Climber ascending in a French valley, with passage blocked, receiving blame

indicators.note: ascending means going up, so in a down answer the pieces are read from the bottom up

parts.note: une is the French for a

indicators.note: blocked means shut off, so the passage is removed from the valley

parts.note: an alley is a narrow passage
a rap is a reprimand or blame, as in take the rap

explanation.surface: A mountaineer climbs a French valley, finds the pass blocked and is blamed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'blocked' takes ALLEY from VALLEY, leaving V; UNE + V + RAP then reads upward, as 'ascending' says.
explanation.definitionFit: A social climber is someone newly risen in society, an upstart: the French-derived word fits exactly.

clue.text: See 14
Austere graduate's in charge …

parts.note: BA is a Bachelor of Arts graduate, and the S is the s of the word

explanation.surface: A newly qualified graduate running things is a spartan sort.
explanation.definitionFit: Basic means plain and without frills, so it serves as a synonym for austere.

clue.text: Reportedly cove's to access material

indicators.note: reportedly means as heard said, so the word is taken by its sound

parts.note: a cove is a bay, and the 's makes it plural

explanation.surface: A bloke (British slang 'cove') is said to have obtained some cloth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cove' is old British slang for a chap, but here it is a small bay; the plural sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the green woollen cloth that covers snooker and card tables, a kind of fabric.

clue.text: The setter's right about going to press

parts.note: the setter refers to himself as I, the 's being is
on means about, concerning

explanation.surface: The puzzle compiler claims to be correct about heading for print.
explanation.definitionFit: To press clothes is to smooth them with a hot iron, so the two verbs are synonyms.

clue.text: … Upright fellow, by all accounts

indicators.note: by all accounts means as people say, so the word is taken by how it sounds

parts.note: a peer is a fellow or equal

explanation.surface: Continuing the last clue, a decent, upright chap, so they say.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Upright' looks like an adjective for the fellow, but it is a noun: a solid vertical support.
explanation.definitionFit: In building this is a vertical pillar or support between openings, an upright.

clue.text: 14's hot

parts.note: the 's can stand for has as well as is
H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps

explanation.walkthrough: The definition is 14 Across's first word, MESS: a muddle. '14's' is read as '14 has', and 'has' plus H for hot gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To make a muddle of something is to bungle or botch it, so the two words are synonyms.

clue.text: Dish sent back as one eats something to fill a gap

indicators.note: eats means takes inside, so the other piece goes in
sent back means returned, so the word as is read backwards

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
a shim is a thin wedge to fill a gap

explanation.surface: A dish returned to the kitchen, eaten by one diner to stave off hunger.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sent back' turns AS into SA; with I that is SAI, which 'eats' SHIM to give the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: This Japanese dish of thinly sliced raw fish is a specific example of a dish.

clue.text: Bull heads for exit, swerving toreador — that's most ingenious

parts.note: neat is an old word for cattle, here a bull

indicators.note: heads means the first letters of the words that follow

explanation.surface: A bull charges for the exit, dodging the matador, a clever move.
explanation.definitionFit: Neat can mean cleverly done, so the superlative means most clever or most deft.

clue.text: Selling everything perhaps that may help students going up or down?

definitions.meaning: emptying your home by selling off its contents

definitions.text: that may help students going up or down?
definitions.meaning: the UK system matching students to spare university places, going up being British for starting university

explanation.surface: A sale of goods to help students moving between levels.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain one 'goes up' to university and 'comes down' at the end; the clearing system finds late places for students.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means an emptying of a whole home of its contents, and also a central agency that matches or distributes things.
